newsitem.title: USA: C-Cor to revamp amid pricing, margin woes.
newsitem.headline: C-Cor to revamp amid pricing, margin woes.

text.p: C-Cor Electronics Inc, which earlier reported sharply lower third quarter earnings, said it will implement a restructuring plan that calls for the transfer of some manufacturing operations to Mexico in the summer of 1997.
The move comes amid profit margins that are being squeezed by excess manufacturing capacity and domestic pricing pressures, the company said.
Under the restructuring plan, C-Cor said the power supply assembly portion of amplifiers, now being produced in C-COR's three Pennsylvania facilities, will be made in Mexico.
C-Cor said it will book a restructuring charge against earnings in its fiscal fourth quarter.
The company said it will further cut back its Reedsville manufacturing facility in an effort to improve gross margins. The move is expected to affect 20 workers.
The plan calls for the restructuring of worldwide sales territories and consolidation of the company's sales forces.
The company also said it will continue to evaluate implementing additional restructuring initiatives.
C-Cor said it is encouraged by ordering and booking trends in recent quarters. It said backlog increased $6.5 million during the third quarter and now stands at $36.4 million.
C-Cor shares were down 1/2 at 9-1/4 in morning trade.
